```{=html}
<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Appendix B <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Proofs &amp; Comments</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">B.14</span> Euler–Lagrange equations (§<a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/length-geodesics.html#subsection_Variations_Euler_Lagrange" data-kind="subsection" data-label="subsection_Variations_Euler_Lagrange">7.2.1</a>)</h1></header>
<p><strong>Setting.</strong> As in Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Metric">7</a>: <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> is smooth, <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma = \pm 1\)</span> on <span class="math inline">\([a,b]\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\gamma([a,b]) \subseteq \mathcal{U}\)</span>, and <span class="math inline">\(\gamma_\mathcal{U} = \mathscr{X} \circ \gamma\)</span>. The Lagrangian <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}\)</span> is defined on the vectors over <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span> with sign <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma\)</span>, <span class="math display">\[
    D \coloneqq \big\{ \mathcal{X}_p \in T\mathcal{U} \;\big|\; \textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, g_p(\mathcal{X}_p, \mathcal{X}_p) &gt; 0 \big\}
    \subseteq T\mathcal{U} \subseteq T\mathcal{M} .
\]</span> Writing <span class="math inline">\((\alpha \, ; \beta) \in \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d\)</span> for the <span class="math inline">\(d\)</span> position slots and the <span class="math inline">\(d\)</span> velocity slots of the bundle chart <span class="math inline">\((T\mathcal{U}, \xi_\mathscr{X})\)</span>, and using <span class="math inline">\(g_p(\mathcal{X}_p, \mathcal{X}_p) = g_{ij}(p) \, x^i_p \, x^j_p\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(p = \mathscr{X}^{-1}(\alpha)\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(x_p = \beta\)</span>, the chart image of <span class="math inline">\(D\)</span> is <span class="math display">\[
    D_\mathscr{X} \coloneqq \xi_\mathscr{X}(D) = \Big\{ (\alpha \, ; \beta) \in \mathscr{X}(\mathcal{U}) \times \mathbb{R}^d \;\Big|\;
    \textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, g_{ij}\big( \mathscr{X}^{-1}(\alpha) \big) \, \beta^i \beta^j &gt; 0 \Big\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d ,
\]</span> and the chart representative of the Lagrangian is <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X} \coloneqq \mathcal{L} \circ \xi_\mathscr{X}^{-1} : D_\mathscr{X} &amp;\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\
    (\alpha \, ; \beta) &amp;\longmapsto \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}(\alpha \, ; \beta) =
    \sqrt{ \textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, g_{ij}\big( \mathscr{X}^{-1}(\alpha) \big) \, \beta^i \beta^j } .
\end{align*}</span> <span class="math inline">\(D_\mathscr{X}\)</span> is open in <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d\)</span>, and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\)</span> is smooth on it, as the square root of a smooth positive function. A point of <span class="math inline">\(D_\mathscr{X}\)</span> is the chart description, through <span class="math inline">\(\xi_\mathscr{X}\)</span>, of a tangent vector with sign <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma\)</span>. For a smooth <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛉ} : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^d\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}(a) = \textrm{\runic ᛉ}(b) = 0\)</span>, the length of <span class="math inline">\(\gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}}\)</span> is <span class="math display">\[
    L_{[a,b]}[\gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}}] = \int_a^b \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\big( \underbrace{\gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}(\lambda)}_{\text{position slots}}
    \, ; \, \underbrace{\dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}'(\lambda)}_{\text{velocity slots}} \big) \, d\lambda ,
\]</span> which makes sense as long as the argument of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\)</span> lies in <span class="math inline">\(D_\mathscr{X}\)</span> for all <span class="math inline">\(\lambda \in [a,b]\)</span>.</p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p><strong>Statement.</strong> <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> is a geodesic if and only if, for <span class="math inline">\(m = 1, \dots, d\)</span> and all <span class="math inline">\(\lambda \in [a,b]\)</span>, <span class="math display">\[
    \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big) \Big]
    - (\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big) = 0 .
\]</span></p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p><strong>Strategy.</strong> The definition of a geodesic is a condition on an <em>integral</em>, for <em>every</em> <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\)</span>. The proof turns it into a condition at <em>every point</em> <span class="math inline">\(\lambda\)</span>, in two moves:</p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li class="dg-labelled"><span class="dg-item-label">(I)</span> <p>compute the derivative at <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0\)</span> (steps 1–4):  <span class="math display">\[
            \frac{d}{d\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} L_{[a,b]}[\gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}}] \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0}
            = \int_a^b \sum_{m=1}^d \left\{ \left[(\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big)
            - \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] \right]  \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m(\lambda)  \right\} \, d\lambda ;
        \]</span></p></li>
<li class="dg-labelled"><span class="dg-item-label">(II)</span> <p>since <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\)</span> is arbitrary, this vanishes for every <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\)</span> if and only if (step 5):  <span class="math display">\[
            \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big) \Big]
            - (\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big) = 0 .
        \]</span></p></li>
</ol>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p><strong>Proof.</strong></p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p><em>The deformed curves are admissible for small <span class="math inline">\(|\textrm{\runic ᛊ}|\)</span>.</em> We need <span class="math inline">\(\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}(\lambda) \, ; \, \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}'(\lambda) \big) \in D_\mathscr{X}\)</span> for all <span class="math inline">\(\lambda \in [a,b]\)</span>. The undeformed points form the compact set <span class="math inline">\(K \coloneqq \big\{ \big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big) \;\big|\; \lambda \in [a,b] \big\} \subseteq D_\mathscr{X}\)</span>. Since <span class="math inline">\(D_\mathscr{X}\)</span> is open, there exist a <span class="math inline">\(\delta &gt; 0\)</span> such that <span class="math inline">\(B_\delta(k) \subseteq D_\mathscr{X}\)</span> for every <span class="math inline">\(k \in K\)</span>, with <span class="math inline">\(B_\delta\)</span> the open balls of the standard topology of <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d = \mathbb{R}^{2d}\)</span>. The deformation keeps each point of <span class="math inline">\(K\)</span> inside its ball as long as  <span class="math display">\[
            \sum_{m=1}^d \Big[ \big( \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m(\lambda) \big)^2 + \big( \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}'^m(\lambda) \big)^2 \Big]
            \leq \textrm{\runic ᛊ}^2 M_\textrm{\runic ᛉ}^2 &lt; \delta^2,
            \qquad
            M_\textrm{\runic ᛉ}^2 \coloneqq \max_{\lambda \in [a,b]} \sum_{m=1}^d \Big[ \big( \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m(\lambda) \big)^2 + \big( \textrm{\runic ᛉ}'^m(\lambda) \big)^2 \Big],
        \]</span>  which holds for <span class="math inline">\(|\textrm{\runic ᛊ}| &lt; \textrm{\runic ᛊ}_0 \coloneqq \delta / (1 + M_\textrm{\runic ᛉ})\)</span>. For such <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛊ}\)</span> the length above is defined, and the function of two variables  <span class="math display">\[
            (\textrm{\runic ᛊ}, \lambda) \longmapsto
            \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}(\lambda) \, ; \, \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}'(\lambda) \big)
        \]</span>  is smooth on <span class="math inline">\((-\textrm{\runic ᛊ}_0, \textrm{\runic ᛊ}_0) \times [a,b]\)</span>, as a composition of smooth maps.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Differentiate under the integral sign.</em> For any <span class="math inline">\(0 &lt; \textrm{\runic ᛊ}_1 &lt; \textrm{\runic ᛊ}_0\)</span>, the partial derivative w.r.t. <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛊ}\)</span> of the function of step 1 is continuous on the compact set <span class="math inline">\([-\textrm{\runic ᛊ}_1, \textrm{\runic ᛊ}_1] \times [a,b]\)</span>, so the derivative and the integral can be exchanged:  <span class="math display">\[
            \frac{d}{d\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} L_{[a,b]}[\gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}}] \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0}
            = \int_a^b \frac{\partial}{\partial \textrm{\runic ᛊ}}
            \Big[ \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}(\lambda) \, ; \, \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}'(\lambda) \big) \Big]_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0} \, d\lambda .
        \]</span></p></li>
<li><p><em>Chain rule.</em> At fixed <span class="math inline">\(\lambda\)</span> (dropped from the notation in this step), <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛊ}\)</span> enters all <span class="math inline">\(2d\)</span> slots of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\)</span>:  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            &amp;\frac{\partial}{\partial \textrm{\runic ᛊ}}
            \Big[ \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ} \, ; \, \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}' \big) \Big]
            \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0}
            \\
            \xlongrightarrow{\text{chain rule}} \;
            &amp;\sum_{m=1}^d \Big[
            \frac{\partial \big( \gamma^m_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m \big)}{\partial \textrm{\runic ᛊ}} \,
            (\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ} \, ; \, \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}' \big)
            + \frac{\partial \big( \dot{\gamma}^m_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}'^m \big)}{\partial \textrm{\runic ᛊ}} \,
            (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ} \, ; \, \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}' \big)
            \Big]
            \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0}
            \\
            \xlongrightarrow{\text{affine in } \textrm{\runic ᛊ}} \;
            &amp;\sum_{m=1}^d \Big[
            \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m \, (\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ} \, ; \, \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}' \big)
            + \textrm{\runic ᛉ}'^m \, (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ} \, ; \, \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} + \textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}' \big)
            \Big]
            \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0}
            \\
            \xlongrightarrow{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} \, = \, 0} \;
            &amp;\sum_{m=1}^d \Big[
            \underbrace{(\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m}_{\text{position shifted by } \textrm{\runic ᛉ}}
            + \underbrace{(\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}'^m}_{\text{velocity shifted by } \textrm{\runic ᛉ}'}
            \Big] .
        \end{align*}</span></p></li>
<li><p><em>Integrate by parts.</em> The functions <span class="math inline">\(\lambda \mapsto (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U}(\lambda) \big)\)</span> are <span class="math inline">\(C^1\)</span> (<span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> are smooth). Inserting step 3 into step 2,  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            &amp;\frac{d}{d\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} L_{[a,b]}[\gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}}] \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0} \\
            \xlongrightarrow{\text{steps 2, 3}} \;
            &amp;\int_a^b \sum_{m=1}^d \Big\{ (\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m
            + (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}'^m \Big\} d\lambda \\
            \xlongrightarrow{\text{product rule}} \;
            &amp;\int_a^b \sum_{m=1}^d \Big\{ (\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m
            + \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m \Big] \\
            &amp; \qquad - \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m \Big\} d\lambda \\
            \xlongrightarrow{\text{fund.\ theorem of calculus}} \;
            &amp;\sum_{m=1}^d \Big[ (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m \Big]_a^b \\
            &amp;+ \int_a^b \sum_{m=1}^d \left\{ \left[(\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big)
            - \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] \right]  \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m(\lambda)  \right\} \, d\lambda \\
            \xlongrightarrow{\textrm{\runic ᛉ}(a) \, = \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}(b) \, = \, 0} \;
            &amp;\int_a^b \sum_{m=1}^d \left\{ \left[(\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big)
            - \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] \right]  \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m(\lambda)  \right\} \, d\lambda .
        \end{align*}</span>  The boundary term is where the fixed endpoints are used.</p></li>
<li><p><em>From the integral to every point.</em> The bracket in the integrand of step 4 is minus the left-hand side of  the Statement, and is continuous in <span class="math inline">\(\lambda\)</span> (<span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> are smooth).</p>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li class="dg-labelled"><span class="dg-item-label">(<span class="math inline">\(\Leftarrow\)</span>)</span> <p>If the Statement holds, the bracket vanishes for every <span class="math inline">\(m\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\lambda\)</span>, so the derivative is <span class="math inline">\(0\)</span>  for every <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\)</span>: <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> is a geodesic.</p></li>
<li class="dg-labelled"><span class="dg-item-label">(<span class="math inline">\(\Rightarrow\)</span>)</span> <p>Suppose, on the contrary, that <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> is a geodesic but the bracket is non-zero for some <span class="math inline">\(m\)</span> at  some <span class="math inline">\(\lambda_0 \in (a,b)\)</span>. Since the derivative of step 4 must vanish for <em>every</em> admissible <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\)</span>, it  must vanish in particular for the bracket itself, multiplied by <span class="math inline">\((\lambda - a)(b - \lambda)\)</span> so as to vanish at the  endpoints:  <span class="math display">\[
                \textrm{\runic ᛉ}^m(\lambda) \coloneqq (\lambda - a)(b - \lambda)
                \Big[ (\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big)
                - \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] \Big] .
            \]</span>  For this choice, each term of the integrand of step 4 is <span class="math inline">\((\lambda - a)(b - \lambda) \geq 0\)</span> times the square of the  bracket. The integrand is therefore non-negative on <span class="math inline">\([a,b]\)</span>, and, by continuity, positive on an interval around  <span class="math inline">\(\lambda_0\)</span>, so  <span class="math display">\[
                \frac{d}{d\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} L_{[a,b]}[\gamma_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}}] \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0}
                = \int_a^b \underbrace{(\lambda - a)(b - \lambda)}_{\geq \, 0} \sum_{m=1}^d
                \underbrace{\Big[ (\partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big)
                - \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ (\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\big( \gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U} \big) \Big] \Big]^2}_{\geq \, 0, \text{ and } &gt; \, 0 \text{ near } \lambda_0} d\lambda &gt; 0 ,
            \]</span>  which contradicts <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span> being a geodesic. Hence the bracket vanishes on <span class="math inline">\((a,b)\)</span> for every <span class="math inline">\(m\)</span>, and on <span class="math inline">\([a,b]\)</span> by  continuity: this is the Statement. <span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p></li>
</ul></li>
</ol>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p>The proof only uses that <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}\)</span> is <span class="math inline">\(C^2\)</span> on an open set containing <span class="math inline">\(K\)</span>. It therefore holds for the action functional <span class="math inline">\(\int_a^b \mathcal{L}\big( v_{\gamma(\lambda)} \big) \, d\lambda\)</span> of any such Lagrangian <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}\)</span>.</p>

```
